fascinating. wonder if our telescopes will one day be powerful enough to directly image some of these first stars. maybe with a space-based one?

If you mean in visible wavelengths, then no. We would not be able to image one of these early stars. Due to redshift, all of their visible wavelengths will be shifted into the infrared and beyond. If you look at the black body radiation profile of a star, their peaks are very close to the visible spectrum and fall off very quickly on the short wavelength side and slowly decay exponentially on the long wavelength side. However we can still image at infrared, microwave and radio wavelengths which can be just as good. In fact in the Radio spectrum we can image very easily with terrestrial based radio telescopes with minimal atmospheric distortion. But infrared and microwave are easily absorbed and scattered in the atmosphere which is why we have space based telescopes such as JWST (which the article is talking about) for infrared and WMAP for microwave.
